subject: Customer audit scope mapping & proposed log attenuation plan
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medhaven.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-21T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Audit kickoff: scope mapping + question about 'log attenuation'

Ben / Naomi,

Thanks again for the time earlier. As we prepare for MedHaven's annual security audit (target window: Aug 2-9), the audit firm asked us to document the data sources used for investigations and to understand any mitigation methods you use to reduce retention footprint while preserving forensics (they used the term "log attenuation").

Can you: 
- Provide a mapping between your SIG/CAIQ controls and the data retention artifacts we would accept as evidence (export formats, TTL stamps, provenance metadata).
- Explain whether you support per-tenant TTL variances or targeted holds (e.g., extend session logs for a specific tenant for 90d).
- Describe any strategies you use that might change the raw log fidelity over time (sampling, aggregated metrics, redaction) and how you can demonstrate chain-of-custody if an auditor requests deleted or aggregated records.

We're asking because our DPO wants the exact list of artifacts to request from you during the audit planning call. No urgency on the first pass, but if you can send a short pack by end of next week that'd be ideal.

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of IT Audit, MedHaven
liam.oconnor@medhaven.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medhaven.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit kickoff: scope mapping + question about 'log attenuation'

Liam — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching an index and a draft retention matrix that maps the typical artifacts we produce (raw token logs, request/response metadata, service traces, KV cache traces) to SIG/SOC2 controls. See attached: sig-evidence-index.csv and log-retention-matrix.pdf.

Short answers up front:
- Per-tenant TTL variance: supported via our Private and Dedicated tiers; we can apply a tenant-specific hold and extend TTL for a defined window (requires a signed MAP and audit ticket).
- Attenuation = sampling/aggregation/redaction: we use a tiered approach — raw request/response captures are kept short (default 30d), we automatically promote artifacts to a secure bucket when flagged for forensics, and anonymous aggregates (metrics) are kept longer. We can provide hashed, salted samples from the secure bucket as evidence with provenance metadata.
- Chain-of-custody: every export is stamped with job id, operator id, and object checksums; we include a manifest (CSV) with the delivered artifacts.

Next steps: Naomi will follow up with the control-to-artifact mapping and an example MAP template. Can we schedule a 30-minute call Thursday to walk the auditor through the evidence formats?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: sig-evidence-index.csv, log-retention-matrix.pdf

Subject: Re: Audit kickoff: scope mapping + question about 'log attenuation'

Liam — adding some detail from the security/evidence side. Apologies for the long note, wanted to be specific about artifacts the auditors typically accept and what we can produce for MedHaven.

1) Evidence artifacts we can produce (examples):
   - Exported request traces (ndjson) with timestamps, request_id, model_id, input/output checksums.
   - System manifests (CSV) listing object paths, export job IDs, operator, and sha256 checksums.
   - Filtered session logs (redacted PII) and corresponding redaction manifests.
   - Snapshot of KV cache metadata (readonly view) for a bounded interval when needed.

2) "Log attenuation" approaches and auditor implications:
   - Tiered retention: raw streams (30d default), secure forensic bucket (90d hold after promotion), aggregated metrics (1y). Promotion to the forensic bucket is operator-initiated (or triggered by an automated alert) and is retained with stricter access controls.
   - Sampling: for high-volume telemetry we store 1:10 sampled raw events + full aggregates; when full-fidelity is required we can perform an immediate export if the original buffer hasn't expired. Sampled exports include sampling seed and method so auditors can reason about coverage.
   - Redaction/obfuscation: we perform deterministic redaction for PII fields and retain manifests that record exactly which keys were redacted so that auditors understand transformation steps.

3) Per-tenant TTL variance / holds:
   - Operationally supported; request requires: (a) signed MAP or PO, (b) support ticket with timestamped request, (c) explicit scope (tenant id + artifact types) and retention period. We log all hold requests and produce a hold manifest.

4) Deliverables we suggest for MedHaven audit:
   - A Control-to-Evidence mapping doc (we'll provide).
   - A sample export (ndjson) for a one-week window with manifest and checksum.
   - A recorded walkthrough with your auditor to show how manifests are generated and verified.

I'll attach a draft MAP template and a short checklist. If you like, we can include a small proof export so the auditors see the format.

Naomi Feldman
Sr. Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: medhaven_map_draft.xlsx

Thanks Naomi — a few clarifying items from our side before we schedule the auditor walkthrough: 

- Please provide the exact list of S3/object paths and table names you would export for a "one-week sample" so we can check data residency and egress policies.
- For the sampling documentation, we need the sampling algorithm description (deterministic? pseudorandom?).
- Chain-of-custody: would you be willing to provide signed manifests (GPG or equivalent) or is the checksum + operator id sufficient? Our auditor has requested signed attestations where possible.

Also, we will need a formal MAP with the PO number and signatures before we ask Redwood to apply any tenant-level TTL changes. Can you confirm the lead time for a TTL variance request (how quickly can the extension be enacted once the MAP is signed)?

Grace Li

Grace — great questions. Short answers and proposed MAP steps below.

- Exact export paths: we will provide a scoped manifest listing the object prefixes and table names for the sample export. Typical prefixes: s3://redwood-prod/forensic-exports/medhaven/<job-id>/ and s3://redwood-logs/tenants/medhaven/requests/YYYY/MM/DD/*. We will enumerate the exact keys in the sample manifest we deliver.
- Sampling algorithm: we use a pseudorandom reservoir sampling seeded by request_id; the sampling seed and method will be included in the sampling manifest so auditors can reproduce the selection.
- Signed manifests: we can provide signed manifests using our internal key signing process (sha256 + signed payload); Naomi will coordinate a signed attestation.
- Lead time for TTL variance: operational lead time is typically 24-48 business hours after a signed MAP + support ticket; emergency hold requests can be actioned in <6 hours with SOC approval. We will record the request and produce a hold manifest with timestamps.

Proposed next steps (Mutual Action Plan):
1) We share Control-to-Evidence mapping doc (by Friday EOD) — Ben
2) MedHaven signs MAP template and returns PO — MedHaven
3) Redwood schedules a 30-min walkthrough with your auditor and delivers a sample export + signed manifest — Redwood
4) If additional fidelity is required, MedHaven submits a TTL variance request per the MAP and we enact the hold — Operational

We'll upload the mapping doc and a small sample export to the Drive link and open a HubSpot ticket (see link in related_links). If that plan works, I'll ask Support to pre-create the hold workflow so lead time is minimized.
